newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan says China shipping deal set - radio.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan says China shipping deal set - radio.

text.p: State-run Taiwan radio said that negotiators from Taiwan and China had reached a "concrete consensus" on Wednesday on ending a ban on direct shipping links between the sides.

"Both sides have reached concrete consensus and signed a summary of the talks in which Taiwan shipping companies can apply immediately to the mainland authorities for links between (Taiwan's) Kaohsiung and (the mainland's) Fuzhou and Xiamen," it said in a report from Hong Kong where the talks were held, quoting Taiwan officials at the talks.
The broadcast gave no clear indication of how the communist mainland government would respond to such applications.

It gave its own estimate that vessels registered in places other than Taiwan and China could begin relevant paperwork after the February 7 Chinese lunar new year and start sailing the two routes across the Taiwan strait in March or April.

Taiwan has banned direct links with the arch rival communist mainland since Chiang Kai-shek's Nationalist Republic of China government lost a civil war to the Chinese communists in 1949 and fled into exile on the island.
Cross-straits shipping now is routed at greater cost through Hong Kong, an arrangement whose future becomes clouded after July 1 when the British colony reverts to Chinese rule.
